title: Open restriction preserves local constancy
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], $F$ a locally constant sheaf of sets on its small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], and $U$ any open subscheme. The set inverse image of $F$ along the inclusion of $U$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] is locally constant on the small etale site of $U$. Neither finite stalks nor Noetherianity is assumed.

proof.text: Choose an etale cover trivializing F on the localized sites and base change it to U. The etale inverse-image restriction comparison identifies the restriction of the pullback sheaf on each base-changed member with the twice-localized restriction of F.

Localization sends a constant sheaf to a constant sheaf: restrict the constant presheaf and use that localization preserves covering families, so its associated sheaf is the localization of the associated constant sheaf. Transport this constancy through the comparison isomorphisms. The base-changed etale cover therefore trivializes the pullback of F. This is the localization/constant-sheaf argument recorded in the declaration docstring; it does not assert finite stalks.
